content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to the Apple assistant, launching with iOS 27. I've noticed it has a clear difference from other AI assistants — and it's the better kind.

iOS 27's all-new Siri doesn't pretend to be human, setting it apart from other AI chatbots

I've been testing Siri AI on iOS 27 beta for nearly two months, and so far it's done everything I expected from it.

The new Siri is a huge improvement over its predecessor, delivering on promises and truly becoming a capable assistant on Apple devices.

But I'll admit that if you need the most powerful, cutting-edge AI tools, rivals like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be better suited for you.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it with these third-party tools, I found one key difference that has me heavily favoring Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go overboard with overly long responses or mimic human-like personalities that slowly build a personal relationship with you.

Siri is practical, intelligent, and does what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It regularly reminds you that it's an AI and may get things wrong. And it doesn't pretend to be your romantic partner.

ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, on the other hand, are all full of personality and opinions, showing more human-like tendencies that feel fake to me.

I imagine some users enjoy that more "personal" approach. But I much prefer AI assistants staying in their lane and not pretending to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not humans. I'm glad Apple understands this and has built the new Siri around that philosophy.

What do you think about how "human-like" AI assistants should be? Let us know in the comments.
